submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent (1.62e-6 A) at Mg 0.58/Mn 0.42. That composition is near Mg7Mn5O12, which has a predicted HSE gap of 2.71 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy. Merit peaked between the spinel and Mg-rich compositions.

rejected.reason: MgMn2O4 spinel region (stable, gap 2.87 eV) measured 1.44e-6 A, lower than index 4
Mg 0.69 measured 1.54e-6 A, lower than index 4
Mn3O4/Mn2O3-type phases have predicted gaps near 0.9 eV, which suggests poor photoanode behaviour; not measured because the budget ran out

consultations.verdict: Support: MgMn2O4 spinel is on the MACE hull (0 eV/atom) and its HSE-level gap (2.87 eV) is below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so it absorbs. Mg-rich Mg6MnO8 gap 3.74 eV would not absorb. Index 22 (Mg 0.353) is closest to spinel stoichiometry.

Support: Mg7Mn5O12 (Mg 0.583, matches index 4 at 0.580) has HSE gap 2.71 eV < 3.22 eV so absorbs, while being more Mg-rich (wider gap than Mn3O4 at 0.94 eV, which likely is a poor photoanode). Mg8Mn3O11 at 3.32 eV would be marginal. Index 4 samples a different region from the spinel measurement.

Support: Mg3MnO4 (Mg 0.75) predicted HSE gap 2.24 eV, absorbing at 3.22 eV; merit rose from spinel (Mg 0.35, 1.44 uA) to Mg 0.58 (1.62 uA), so extending toward the Mg-rich Mg7Mn5O12/Mg3MnO4 region (index 8, Mg 0.69) tests the upward trend.
